_doc: Sanitizer rule-spec — the ONE machine-readable source of truth for the
content rules shared by the Go DB sanitizer (internal/core/sanitize.go,
which embeds this file) and the Python harvest sanitizer
(scripts/harvest_fixtures.py, which reads it from the repo).
Neither implementation may carry its own copy of these tables.
The two implementations deliberately DIFFER beyond these rules: the
harvest script additionally pseudonymizes ids, aliases project paths and
salts the placeholder hash, because its output is published as committed
fixtures; the DB sanitizer keeps ids and paths verbatim with an unsalted
hash, because the DB is local-first. Those harvest-only behaviors use
Contract vectors live in testdata/sanitizer-vectors/; both
implementations must produce byte-identical output over them
content_keys_doc: values that are content by definition — always stripped to a placeholder, any length: strings, objects and arrays (an entire tool_use input object becomes one placeholder). NUMBERS, BOOLEANS and NULL pass through content keys verbatim — they cannot carry prompt/response text, and generic key names collide across formats (OpenCode's tokens.input/tokens.output are numbers under the same names as Claude Code's tool input and Codex's tool output; stripping them broke ccusage totals — caught by the opencode harvest self-check, M2 Task 4). Includes short content-bearing fields found in real logs that slip under the max_free_len rule (aiTitle, lastPrompt, subject, description). The second group was added for Codex rollout records (M2 Task 3: tool args/outputs, exec command lines and outputs, patch diffs keyed by real paths, instruction blobs, reasoning ciphertext, web-search queries/urls, guardian rationale, error info). The third group was added for OpenCode message rows (M2 Task 4: provider error response bodies/headers, diff patches, system prompts).
string_content_keys_doc: keys whose STRING values are stripped but whose list/dict values keep their structure and are recursed into. 'content': the message.content block array. 'message': Codex carries full message text as a string under this key (agent_message/user_message/error), while Claude Code's 'message' is the structural object holding usage — strip strings, recurse structures.
safe_keys_doc: keys whose string values are known-safe metadata at any length (ids, timestamps, models, ...). The harvest sanitizer still pseudonymizes id-shaped and aliases path-shaped values regardless of this list.
max_free_len_doc: unknown string fields longer than this many UTF-8 BYTES are stripped; at or under it they pass through (a pure length threshold is not a content filter — newly observed free-text keys go into content_keys).

placeholder.doc: the stripped-content marker. len = UTF-8 byte length of the hashed input; hash = first hash_hex_chars lowercase hex chars of sha256(salt_utf8 + input_utf8). The DB sanitizer uses an empty salt; the harvest sanitizer salts per harvest. Non-string values are first encoded per nonstring_encoding; strings hash their raw UTF-8 bytes.
placeholder.nonstring_encoding: canonical JSON: object keys sorted, compact separators (',' ':'), non-ASCII unescaped (raw UTF-8), no HTML escaping
placeholder.idempotency: a string already matching regex passes through every sanitizer verbatim, even under content keys

id_shapes.doc: string shapes treated as opaque identifiers: kept verbatim by the DB sanitizer, pseudonymized shape-preservingly by the harvest sanitizer.

pathlike_doc: a string is path-shaped when it starts with '/' or '~', or starts with '.' and contains '/', or contains '/' and no whitespace. Path-shaped values pass through the DB sanitizer verbatim and are aliased segment-wise by the harvest sanitizer.

harvest.doc: tables used only by the harvest sanitizer's aliasing layer (committed-fixture publication); the DB sanitizer ignores this section.
harvest.path_keyed_maps_doc: maps whose keys are file paths BY SCHEMA: every key is tokenized to p-<8hex>[.ext] unconditionally — no path-likeness heuristics (extensionless keys like 'Makefile' must not slip through). The leak checker enforces the same set on committed fixtures.
harvest.git_branch_keys_doc: keys holding a git branch name (Claude Code: gitBranch; Codex session_meta git block: branch).
harvest.git_branch_allowlist_doc: git-branch values kept verbatim; everything else becomes branch-<6hex>.
harvest.path_segment_allowlist_doc: STRUCTURAL path segments carrying no project identity, kept verbatim BEFORE the project segment only; every segment after the project segment becomes a sanitizer token. The second group is well-known agent/tool/XDG dir names (OS- or tool-created, public software names) observed in real Codex logs (M2) — without them the alias map collides with the repo's own docs naming the same tools. Structural names need no owner ruling.
harvest.owner_approved_segments_doc: OWNER-APPROVED EXCEPTIONS, distinct from structural names: owner-CREATED directory names default to aliasing and stay verbatim only after an explicit owner ruling reviewing that the name carries no project identity. NTFY: ruled harmless 2026-06-11 (ntfy push-notification tooling directory). serve: ruled harmless 2026-06-11 (common dictionary word, zero identity content; collided with its common-word use in prose). images: owner-APPROVED 2026-06-11 under the dictionary-word rule (collided with public /v1/images/generations endpoint paths in the committed LiteLLM price snapshot). Decision rule: structural (OS/tool-created) names go in path_segment_allowlist without a ruling; owner-created names go here ONLY with a recorded ruling — common-dictionary-word segments may be owner-approved on collision, distinctive/coined names default to aliasing.
harvest.owner_approved_values_doc: owner rulings on VALUES kept verbatim (these pass the sanitizer via the short-string/safe-key rules; the entry records the explicit review, same category as owner_approved_segments). 2026-06-11: all OpenCode provider/model identifiers — vllm-* including vllm-tecnigmaai-nvfp4 — reviewed as vLLM serving-recipe names, not personal identity.
harvest.path_segment_allowlist_regexes_doc: segment patterns that are structural wherever they appear: purely numeric segments are date-tree components (Codex stores sessions under sessions/YYYY/MM/DD), never project identity.
harvest.verbatim_value_keys_doc: keys whose string values are closed-vocabulary metadata kept verbatim even when slash-shaped (IANA timezones look like paths and must not be aliased into fake project names).
